source.title: SafeMERGE: Preserving Safety Alignment in Fine-Tuned Large Language Models via Selective Layer-Wise Model Merging
source.authors: Aladin Djuhera; S. Kadhe; Farhan Ahmed; Syed Zawad; Holger Boche

record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes aligned chat/instruct models on harmful or ordinary task data and measures harmful outputs, but uses LoRA fine-tuning and its own prompt benchmarks and safety classifiers rather than reproducing the original study methods exactly.
record.gate_note: The study directly reports harmfulness after harmful-data fine-tuning and compares harmfulness before and after ordinary utility-task fine-tuning. Results for SafeMERGE and other defenses are not rows here: they assess those methods rather than testing the claim versions about fine-tuning or token depth.
record.test_reason: The study LoRA fine-tunes four aligned chat/instruct models on benign task data (GSM8K, PubMedQA, three telecom sets) and on harmful data (AdvBench, HarmfulQA). It measures Llama-Guard-3 harmfulness on DirectHarm and HexPhi. This bears directly on V2, and on V1 through the harmful checkpoints built for RESTA. The methods differ from the originals: LoRA only, its own benchmarks, and a guard-model judge.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors take as given, citing prior work, that benign fine-tuning erodes safety; their own results show it across four models and five tasks. Their conclusion centers on SafeMERGE restoring safety with negligible utility cost. They do not analyze token depth.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests ordinary utility-task LoRA fine-tuning (and separately harmful-data LoRA tuning), using DirectHarm and HexPhi with guard-model harmfulness scores; the text does not establish that these procedures match the original studies exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: Harmfulness increases differ by model and fine-tuning dataset; the study reports classifier-based scores and notes that thresholds are tuned on test sets for the main experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Merging a subset of LoRA layers (as few as about 8 of 56–64) with a safety-tuned adapter substantially lowers harmfulness after benign fine-tuning. Layers are chosen by cosine similarity to the aligned-minus-base weight difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc safety restoration needs intervention on only a minority of fine-tuned layers.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Safety is evaluated using classifier-based harmfulness scores. The harmful-data fine-tuning table gives no untreated comparison and does not state training-example counts. The authors report that main safety-benchmark hyperparameters are tuned on test sets because separate validation splits are unavailable; they provide a held-out split check for one setting.
record.rows_left_out: Defense-only SafeMERGE, SafeInstruct, RESTA, RESTA-Instruct, and SafeLoRA outcome comparisons and their ablations were not extracted as claim rows; they evaluate defense performance rather than the versions cataloged here.

untested.parts: Number of harmful examples is not stated (full AdvBench/HarmfulQA sets implied, 5 epochs). The 'few to a few hundred' scale is not tested, and full-parameter fine-tuning is not tested.
Only LoRA (q,v; rank 8) is used. Few-example or deliberately selected benign data is not tested, and no dose-response is reported.
Not tested; the authors explicitly exclude jailbreak and prefill attacks.
Not tested causally. Layer-selective merging is a defense, not a localization test.

missing.what: Untuned-model harmfulness scores, which serve as baselines for the harmful fine-tuning rows (same models, benchmarks and judge)
ShieldGemma-9B cross-check of original versus fine-tuned harmfulness, showing consistent increases (e.g. Llama-2 GSM8K DirectHarm 4.50→27.30)

record.verdict_notes: The harmful fine-tuning results are a by-product of building RESTA's harmful vector, but they directly measure harmful compliance after harmful tuning, and the untuned baselines come from Table 1 under the same evaluator. Example counts are not stated. No uncertainty is reported, so small increases on HexPhi may be within noise. Hyperparameters for defenses were tuned on test sets, but this does not affect the original-vs-fine-tuned comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful fine-tuning results do not state training-example counts or compare the harmful-data-tuned checkpoints with their corresponding untuned checkpoints.
The study tests ordinary utility-task fine-tuning, not a systematic range of benign datasets or few-example fine-tuning.
Selective layer-wise merging is proposed as a defense, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks causally carries safety behaviour.

tranche.reason: Own results test fine-tuning-induced harmfulness using LoRA, DirectHarm/HexPhi and guard-model evaluation, addressing the same question with a different experimental recipe.

source_check.notes: Harmfulness is the percentage of responses flagged unsafe by Llama-Guard-3-8B; harmful tuning uses five epochs but gives no example count, so few-example susceptibility is untested. The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated 23 Apr 2026.
